title: Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic
main_claim: Let X be a projective Q-factorial terminal threefold over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>3. If K_X is nef with nu(K_X)=1, then K_X is semiample and kappa(X,K_X)=1. The proof argues by contradiction in the case of maximal nef dimension. That case yields a prepared nef cycle D on a smooth threefold V. Jet and Laurent-cohomology calculations then make Pic of the punctured formal neighbourhood p-divisible, while intersection with H gives a nonzero homomorphism from that group to Z, with degree D·H^2>0.

issues.location: slopes.tex, Prop. strong-semistability (bend-and-break step); cartier.tex final proof; preparation.tex MMP steps
issues.description: Some load-bearing inputs are recent results that cannot be checked from the paper: the quantitative bend-and-break bound N·Gamma <= (dim+1) N·C/(-K·C) for curves in the smooth locus of a normal projective W in any characteristic [jlr2026, Thm 1.1]; the nef-dimension-at-most-two abundance theorem [xu2024, Thm 1.8]; and the nef reduction and partial MMP with restored boundary [xu2026]. The paper uses them consistently with the hypotheses it states for them, but their exact statements could not be checked against the sources.
issues.evidence: "We use the following quantitative form of bend-and-break \cite[Theorem~1.1]{jlr2026}: ... This statement is valid in arbitrary characteristic."

coverage:
I read the whole LaTeX source: introduction, preparation, slopes, jets, laurent and cartier. Steps checked in detail:
- Preparation: the lct and dlt modification; the (K+B-eps S)-MMP isolating S_Y (anti-nef restriction gives disjointness); the support claim for the second dlt modification; the local-cohomology lemma extending torsion across finitely many points (connecting-map injectivity, the t^{j-1} kill argument); the Kummer cover and the p^b-canonical section supported on D; Hodge-index proportionality D ≡ cN_tot.
- Slopes: the foliation canonical formula sign, checked on the case F=T_{P^1}; the rank-1 and rank-2 bracket and p-closure slope inequalities; the bend-and-break degree ratio p·D·H^2/(Lambda·H^2 + t·Lambda·H·D); the strong-semistability induction; Langer's Bogomolov inequality with the tuple (H,D); the Hom/section bounds and the absence of scalar polar parts.
- Jets: the page calculus, including the Serre-duality index P^s_j -> P^s_{s-j}(E^!) and the middle recurrence; the periodic Euler identity; HRR giving the per-layer Euler characteristic D·c2/12 (D^3, D^2K and DK^2 terms vanish); the scalar jet rule; the forced canonical jets; the canonical formal root (P | b_alpha); the residue-swap derivation of a*=p/(p+1) and D·c2=0.
- Laurent: the phase-bound constants (I checked with sympy that 2a*-1-(1-2/p) = 2/(p(p+1)), and that the choice of lambda and m in {1,2} works for p>=5); in Thm laurent-vanishing, the drop rule (k<2d_e, the matching margins, j-independence via alpha'=q*alpha+(1-q)*beta), the middle-row count over at most two occupied lifts, the fixed-weight vanishing and the bound B_l on the primitives' upper cuts; the HRR condition (i) for Omega (the D-terms reduce to D·(K^2-3c2)/4 = 0) and for B^1; conditions (ii) and (iii) for B^1 and (B^1)^! via F_*.
- Cartier: H^0(Z^1)=W and bijectivity of C; surjectivity of C-id via a finite map of P^n (Lang-type); the Cartier-fixed connection; the rank-one p-curvature identity; Katz horizontal expansion; extension of line bundles over the regular completion; the unit-order sequence and flasqueness; descent of Phi, and the contradiction between p-divisibility and Phi(O(H)) = D·H^2.
I did not independently verify the cited external theorems (jlr2026, xu2024, xu2026, posva2024, Cossart-Piltant).
